keyFindings.description: DrainSubscription's awaitBindLocked has no deadline, so a restore's bind (up to 10 s) in flight when the stop begins can push the stop to about signal + 20 s in a double fault (late subscribe and a connection replacement together); handlers are still given up at signal + 15 s and the shutdown stays inside the 25 s document budget. The same wait existed in round 2's Release.

The legacy multi-subject durable replacement runs DeleteConsumer then AddConsumer under the stop deadline; a deadline between them leaves no durable, and the next holder recreates it with DeliverAll (a stream replay of idempotent upserts, not lost messages). Needs a legacy durable still present and a reconcile straddling signal + 15 s; an AddConsumer timeout already produced the same state.
